chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:
A fire will be kindled for them, and it will be said to them, 'Enter it.' If they enter it, it will be cool and peaceful for them. But if they refuse,
Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say to them: 'Behold, I had commanded you, and you disobeyed Me.'
Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will command that they be taken to the Fire.

key_terms.أَمَرْتُكُمْ: I commanded you, indicating divine instruction
key_terms.ادْخُلُوهَا: enter it, a divine command to enter the fire
key_terms.بَرْدًا: coolness, meaning the fire would not harm them
key_terms.تُؤَجَّجُ: will be kindled or set ablaze
key_terms.فَعَصَيْتُمُونِي: you disobeyed Me, referring to refusal of Allah's command
key_terms.نَارٌ: a fire, representing the means of testing and punishment

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe Allah's test and judgment in the afterlife?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a test involving the people mentioned in the chapter, in which obedience to Allah determines their outcome. It highlights divine justice in the afterlife and shows that submission to Allah's command brings safety, while disobedience leads to punishment.
